account: Lenovo's release of 15 October 2024 reports that Erin Taylor, a disability advocate with ALS, used the technology to introduce herself and welcome Lenovo Chairman and CEO Yuanqing Yang to the stage at Tech World. She spoke through an avatar in a recreation of her voice as it sounded before her diagnosis. Lenovo co-developed the system and calls it a proof of concept in testing. On 18 March 2025 ALS Network, a patient charity, confirmed that Erin Taylor spoke at Tech World with eye gaze and her AI avatar. In the ITU entry, current to June 2025, the Scott-Morgan Foundation reports that its communication platform enabled Erin Taylor to introduce Lenovo's CEO at Tech World. The chapter also describes an Austrian former parliamentarian and a father who use related communication tools. The sources do not establish a lasting restoration of independent communication. On 15 December 2025 Observer reported that the foundation had launched a successor platform, VoXAI, at the AI Summit New York. The foundation built it with D-ID, ElevenLabs, Irisbond, Lenovo and Nvidia. Observer reported that VoXAI is free at the basic tier, with advanced features available for a $30 monthly subscription. Observer interviewed users with ALS who communicate through it.
